clue.text: Written assurance offered as cautious about storm

indicators.note: about says the word for cautious goes round the word for storm

parts.note: a cautious person is wary
to storm in anger is to rant

explanation.surface: A guarantee is handed over by someone nervous about bad weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarantee from a seller, set down on paper, promising repair or replacement.

clue.text: Hints may be very loud in card game finishing early

indicators.note: in says the music marking goes inside the card game
finishing early means the last letter of the game is cut off

parts.note: whist is a trick-taking card game
FF, fortissimo, is the music marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Clues can be very noisy in a card game that ends early.
explanation.definitionFit: A faint trace or suggestion of something, as of scandal, is a hint of it.

clue.text: Aren't I excited, being a bit of a looker?

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters of the phrase are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they are thrilled to be thought attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram ignores the apostrophe. 'looker' seems to mean an attractive person; it is an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye is one part of the organ that looks.

clue.text: Part of stage raised by some minor party

indicators.note: raised says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A section of a stage is lifted by a small political party.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' reads the letters upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The forestage in front of the curtain in a theatre is called by this name.

clue.text: Crawlers two bad drivers regularly ignored

indicators.note: regularly ignored means every other letter is dropped, keeping the first, third and so on

explanation.surface: Two poor drivers creep along the road and are often overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crawlers' suggests slow cars; it means flatterers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sycophants who fawn on the powerful are said to crawl to them.

clue.text: Scandinavian mainly going after Massachusetts properties

indicators.note: going after says the shortened Scandinavian word is placed behind the state abbreviation

parts.note: MA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Massachusetts

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: Norse describes the old peoples and language of Scandinavia

explanation.surface: A Nordic buyer chases after property in Massachusetts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' trims NORSE to NORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Landed estates with a big house are traditionally called by this word in Britain.

clue.text: Justify a record in composure

indicators.note: in says the record sits inside the word for composure

parts.note: poise is calm composure
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: Someone defends a disc in a calm way.
explanation.walkthrough: The sense is the older one of arguing in defence of something, as in an apologia.
explanation.definitionFit: In its old sense the verb means to argue in defence of something, as an apologist does.

clue.text: Sort of music speaker icon, oddly

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker

indicators.note: oddly picks the letters in odd positions, the first and third

explanation.surface: A strange kind of music comes from a speaker icon on a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes I and O from 'icon'.
explanation.definitionFit: A large choral work on a sacred theme, such as Handel's Messiah, is a kind of music.

clue.text: Novel newly penned by Stallone is carelessly done

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so the actor's nickname goes round the jumbled letters

parts.note: Sly is the nickname of the actor Sylvester Stallone

indicators.note: newly means made new, so the letters of novel are rearranged

explanation.surface: A novel just written by Stallone is sloppy work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like the book; it is the anagram fodder that 'newly' reworks.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidy, sloppy and slapdash in work or appearance.

clue.text: Blessed with time for fine home

indicators.note: with X for Y says one letter replaces another inside the word

parts.note: blessed is used ironically for cursed or damned, as in 'this blessed rain', like infernal
F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Someone blessed with time on their hands swaps a fine for a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blessed' is ironic here, the way 'blasted' or 'infernal' is; swap the F for a T.
explanation.definitionFit: Home affairs and home news are domestic, the inside matters of a country.

clue.text: Party set missing source of inky fish

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: missing says a letter is taken out of the word for set

parts.note: a radio set

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A party lacks its ink-producing fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops the I (from 'source of inky') from RADIO, leaving RADO.
explanation.definitionFit: A golden game species found in warm seas, also called mahi-mahi.

clue.text: Worry generated by guitar bar?

definitions.meaning: to fuss anxiously or be uneasy
one of the raised ridges across a guitar's neck

explanation.surface: Anxiety caused by a part of a guitar.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb for being anxious and the ridge on a fingerboard share this word.

clue.text: Pigeon lover welcoming home banker

indicators.note: welcoming means letting someone in, so the pigeon lover goes round the word for home

parts.note: a pigeon fancier keeps and breeds pigeons
in means at home

explanation.surface: A pigeon keeper invites a banker into his loft.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who handles large money deals and investment is a banker in the broad sense.

clue.text: Gas found in Australia once carbon is extracted

parts.note: Oz is an informal name for Australia

indicators.note: extracted means pulled out, so the letter for carbon is removed from the word once

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A gas found in Australia used to contain carbon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is extracted' removes C from ONCE, leaving ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A form of oxygen with three atoms per molecule, the layer that screens out ultraviolet.

clue.text: Book performances

definitions.meaning: the ... of the Apostles is a book of the New Testament
turns on a variety bill are performances

explanation.surface: Someone books a series of shows.
explanation.definitionFit: A biblical book name and the turns given by entertainers share this word.

clue.text: Cold interior to be renovated as standard

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold

indicators.note: renovated means done up and remade, so the letters of interior are reordered

explanation.surface: A chilly room inside is to be done up to a proper standard.
explanation.definitionFit: A test or measure by which things are judged is a standard.

clue.text: Tense opponent must accept one is insignificant

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the opponent goes round the numeral for one

parts.note: a rival is an opponent
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A nervous competitor has to admit that someone is unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective for the opponent; it is just T. 'must accept' puts I inside RIVAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Petty, of no real importance or weight.

clue.text: Commercial property assumptions taken as true

definitions.meaning: a building and its land used by a business
statements accepted as the basis for an argument

explanation.surface: Shop buildings and the beliefs about them taken for granted.
explanation.definitionFit: A business's buildings and the starting points of an argument share this plural.

clue.text: Recognise and deny if it changes

indicators.note: changes means the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spots something and rejects it if it alters.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick out and name someone or something, as a witness does in a line-up.

clue.text: Drink producing audible complaint by Bolshevik

parts.note: a red is a communist, like the Bolsheviks of the Russian Revolution

indicators.note: audible means heard, so the word for complaint is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: a whine is a peevish complaint

explanation.surface: A Bolshevik grumbles loudly over a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret, merlot and other grape wines of that colour are a drink.

clue.text: Naked jumper's language

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters are removed

parts.note: a jersey is a jumper, the British word for a knitted sweater

explanation.surface: A streaker's tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naked' strips the outer letters J and Y from JERSEY. It is the Gaelic of Ireland or Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The old name for Irish or Scottish Gaelic, a Celtic tongue.

clue.text: A great deal may be killed

definitions.meaning: a large amount or number, as in a whole lot of problems
the old past tense of slay, meaning killed

explanation.surface: Lots of people may be put to death.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word is a noun for a large quantity and the past of slay.

clue.text: Food blog designed to support resort

indicators.note: in a down clue the jumbled letters sit below the resort, holding it up

parts.note: a spa is a health resort

indicators.note: designed means arranged anew, so the letters of blog are reordered

explanation.surface: A food blog set up to promote a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' turns BLOG into GBOL, placed under SPA. Spag bol is British slang for spaghetti bolognese.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti with a meat sauce, shortened in British slang, is a common dish.

clue.text: Ships millions hoarded by a school for actors

indicators.note: hoarded means stored away, so the letter for millions is held inside

parts.note: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London

explanation.surface: A drama school stashes away millions to buy boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hoarded by' puts M inside A RADA.
explanation.definitionFit: A great fleet of warships, like the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Case of sow on heat, possibly — a broad area

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters
possibly means the letters of heat may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A pig in season roams over a wide area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case of' gives SW; 'possibly' turns HEAT into ATHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide strip or expanse of land, as in a swathe of countryside.

clue.text: Rodents will eat last of rotten food

indicators.note: eating takes something in, so the rodents go round the final letter

parts.note: mice are small rodents

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of rotten

explanation.surface: Mice will nibble the remains of food that has gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will eat' puts N inside MICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Minced beef or the fruit filling of a mince pie, both foods.

clue.text: Brainless model's second caution about racket?

parts.note: caution is care taken
C stands for circa, meaning about
a racket is a noisy row

explanation.surface: A dim fashion model is warned a second time about a noisy party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' here is circa, C, not a containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The straw figure in a field has no brain, like the one in The Wizard of Oz.

clue.text: Winter generally protects this bird flying north

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards
protects means the words hold the bird's letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Winter usually shelters a bird migrating north.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'this bird' points to the answer itself within the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A white wading heron is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Character's presence

definitions.meaning: spunk or mettle, as in a team showing great character
a ghostly being felt in a room

explanation.surface: A person's force of personality.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: courage and verve, and a ghost sensed nearby.

clue.text: Live in Scottish island with time to be perverse

indicators.note: in says the word for live sits inside the island

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: Settling on a Scottish island for a while is a contrary thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde, off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Straying from what is normal or right, the deviant behaviour of a wayward person.

clue.text: Staggering — eschewing wife's maxim!

indicators.note: eschewing means avoiding, so the letter for wife is left out

parts.note: staggering is swaying on one's feet
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: An astonishing proverb from someone avoiding marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staggering' looks like 'amazing'; it is the swaying of a drunk. 'eschewing' drops W.
explanation.definitionFit: An adage or proverb is a short, familiar statement of wisdom.

clue.text: Meat cooked by boring lodger perhaps

parts.note: something flat is dull and boring

indicators.note: cooked means the letters of meat are prepared in a new order

explanation.surface: A dull lodger cooks meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sharing rented rooms with you is one example of a lodger.
